{{Short description|Swedish physicist}}
'''Per Carlqvist''' (born July 25, 1938, in [[Stockholm]], [[Sweden]]) is a Swedish plasma physicist with an interest in astrophysical applications.<ref>Biographical information from: Carlqvist, Per; Gahm, Gosta F., "[http://adsabs.harvard.edu/cgi-bin/nph-bib_query?bibcode=1992ITPS...20..867C&amp;db_key=AST&amp;data_type=HTML&amp;format=&amp;high=42ca922c9c02593 Manifestations of electric currents in interstellar molecular cloud]" (1992) ''IEEE Transactions on Plasma Science'' (ISSN 0093-3813), vol. 20, no. 6, p. 867-873.</ref> In 1963, he received the degree of ''civilingenjör'' from the [[Royal Institute of Technology]], [[Stockholm]]; in 1970, the Tekn. lic.; and in 1980 the Tekn. D.

He is currently affiliated with the Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, at the School of Electrical Engineering in the department of Space & Plasma Physics.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120730010005/http://www.ee.kth.se/php/index.php?action=people&cmd=extended&peopleid=421|title=Web page}} of Per Calqvist</ref>

He is the author of several papers on [[astrophysical plasmas]], from the formation of stars, [[Double layer (plasma)|double layers]], the [[Bennett Pinch]], to interstellar helical filaments. 

==The Carlqvist Relation==
Carlqvist lends his name to the "[[Bennett_Pinch#The Carlqvist relation|Carlqvist Relation]]",<ref>[[Gerrit_Verschuur|Gerrit L. Verschuur]], "[https://doi.org/10.1007%2FBF00678079 Interstellar neutral hydrogen filaments at high galactic latitudes and the bennett pinch]" (1995) Volume 227, Numbers 1-2 / May, 1995</ref> a formula used in plasma physics to describe how an electrically conducting plasma filament is compressed by magnetic forces to form a "[[Pinch (plasma physics)|plasma pinch]]". Carlqvist noted that by using his relation, and a derivative, it is possible to describe the Bennett pinch, the [[Jeans Instability|Jeans criterion]] (for gravitational instability,<ref>J. H. Jeans, "[http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1902RSPTA.199....1J The stability of a spherical nebula]" ''Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. A ''199 (1902)</ref> in one and two dimensions), [[Birkeland current|force-free magnetic fields]], gravitationally balanced magnetic pressures, and continuous transitions between these states.<ref>Carlqvist, Per, "[http://adsabs.harvard.edu/cgi-bin/nph-bib_query?1988Ap&SS.144...73C Cosmic electric currents and the generalized Bennett relation]" (1988) ''Astrophysics and Space Science'' (ISSN 0004-640X), vol. 144, no. 1-2, May 1988, p. 73-84</ref>
